title: 25 Centavos

obverse.description: The country name above the Guatemalan coat of arms (two laurel branches around a quetzal bird perched on a scroll and the phrase "Libertad 15 De Setiembre De 1821" written on the scroll along with two rifles and two swords crossed behind the scroll) and the date below
obverse.lettering:
REPUBLICA DE GUATEMALA
LIBERTAD
15 DE
SETIEMBRE
DE 1821
1988
obverse.lettering_translation:
Republic of Guatemala
Liberty
15th of
September
1821

reverse.description: Native bust facing left with the value to the right and bottom-right

comments:
Images of the different coins with their km# from 1977-2000

 

KM# 278.1 - No outlined coat. Portrait #1. "25" in italic.
KM# 278.2 - Outlined coat. Portrait #2. "25" in italic.
KM# 278.3 - No outlined coat. Portrait #3. "25" in italic.
KM# 278.4 - Coat with outlined scroll. Portrait #4. "25" in italic.
KM# 278.5 - No outlined coat. Different portraits. "25" in roman. Varieties in number of wing feathers and in head details.
KM# 278.6 - No outlined coat. Different portraits. "25" in roman. This variant would be the only accepted variant for legal tender currency; because after the 1997 monetary reform all older coins fell in disuse, they can be easily exchanged at banks, but stores won't accept them because of the outdated designs. Most denominations got new types because of this reform, but in this coin's case the same coin had a design revision rather than a complete type change. Machines would mostly only accept the reeded version of this variant because of this.
